learningObjectives: Distinguish synchronous execution from asynchronous execution.
Use async and await for I/O-bound operations.
Understand tasks, event loops, and concurrency trade-offs.

activities.title: Async Execution Model
activities.instruction: Explore the components that make asynchronous execution possible.

content.concept: Python's asyncio model uses an event loop to coordinate coroutines and tasks, allowing other work to progress while an operation is awaiting I/O.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: A coroutine is an awaitable computation defined with async def.
The async keyword defines a coroutine function.
await suspends the current coroutine until the awaited operation can continue.
A Task schedules a coroutine to run concurrently with other tasks.
The event loop coordinates and runs asynchronous tasks and callbacks.

activities.title: Concurrent Task Flow
activities.instruction: Arrange the steps for running multiple asynchronous tasks.

content.concept: Multiple I/O-bound coroutines can be scheduled as tasks so the event loop can make progress on another task while one is waiting.

activities.title: Concurrency Strategy
activities.instruction: Choose the execution approach that fits the scenario.

content.concept: Async programming is particularly useful for I/O-bound workloads. CPU-heavy work generally requires different concurrency or parallelism strategies.
